threads.body: [General] This blanket exclusion treats genuine class type-parameter changes as compatible as well as japicmp false positives. Removing the type parameter from `Api<T>` produces `CLASS_GENERIC_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`, so the gate accepts it even though consumers using `Api<String>` no longer compile. Limit the allowance to identified false-positive members or changes instead of disabling this compatibility check globally.

replies.body: Fixed in 147f3056b6c7bd5121c6b0adc8863f305f162e50. The blanket CLASS_GENERIC_TEMPLATE_CHANGED exclusion is gone. The source rule now permits the specific case of newly added class type parameters, and the regression test checks that removing GenericClass<T>'s parameter is rejected.

threads.body: [Build] This exclusion suppresses genuine inherited abstract-method incompatibilities, not just inherited-default-method false positives. For example, making an existing public abstract class implement `Runnable` without implementing `run()` breaks downstream concrete subclasses, but the resulting `METHOD_ABSTRACT_ADDED_IN_IMPLEMENTED_INTERFACE` change is accepted. Replace the blanket exclusion with a member-aware allowance that verifies an actual inherited default implementation.

replies.body: Fixed in 147f3056b6c7bd5121c6b0adc8863f305f162e50 by removing the inherited-abstract-method exclusion. Regression fixtures check that adding an unimplemented Runnable contract is rejected and that inherited default implementations remain compatible.

threads.body: [Build] Generic-only signature changes, such as changing a return type from `List<String>` to `List<Integer>`, can remain `UNCHANGED` in japicmp 0.23.1 while being source-incompatible. `UnchangedMemberRule` records these members as seen before the new source-incompatibility rule runs, allowing the API break to pass `check`. Register the source-incompatibility rule for `UNCHANGED` before `UnchangedMemberRule`.

replies.body: Fixed in 147f3056b6c7bd5121c6b0adc8863f305f162e50. SourceIncompatibleRule now runs for UNCHANGED members before UnchangedMemberRule. The regression test verifies that changing List<String> to List<Integer> is rejected even though japicmp reports the method as UNCHANGED.

@copilot Update this PR directly to finish the requested build-enforced stable API compatibility port. Copilot review 5646635524 identified three potential enforcement holes. Assess them against the actual japicmp-gradle-plugin 0.4.6 and japicmp 0.23.1 behavior, reproduce representative cases, and fix the confirmed holes with focused regression coverage. Preserve legitimate compatible changes and applicable core behavior; do not implement speculative complex allowances when a simpler correct solution works.

The confirmed rule-ordering concern is that UnchangedMemberRule records every UNCHANGED member as seen before generic SourceIncompatibleRule can inspect it. ViolationsGenerator processes status rules before generic rules, and AbstractRecordingSeenMembers skips seen members. Ensure genuinely source-incompatible generic-only signature changes, such as List<String> to List<Integer> return types, cannot bypass the gate merely because japicmp reports UNCHANGED. Register source-incompatibility handling ahead of unchanged-member suppression as appropriate and test it.

The other two review findings concern compatibilityChangeExcludes entries copied from core. CLASS_GENERIC_TEMPLATE_CHANGED may also suppress real breaks such as removing the parameter from Api<T>. METHOD_ABSTRACT_ADDED_IN_IMPLEMENTED_INTERFACE may suppress a real break when an existing public abstract class starts implementing Runnable without implementing run(), breaking downstream concrete subclasses. Verify these concrete cases. If they are real bypasses, narrow or remove only the problematic blanket allowances while preserving demonstrated generic false positives and inherited-default compatibility. Keep both intended allowances for adding default methods and converting abstract methods to default. Do not dismiss a demonstrated API break solely because core has the same exclusion. If a finding is factually incorrect, leave code unchanged and explain the concrete reproduction evidence in your task outcome.

Validate that the unmodified current stable modules still pass against the pinned baseline, a representative binary break and each confirmed source break fail, and compatible/default-method and AutoValue changes still pass as relevant. Keep temporary probe changes out of the final diff. Use existing build-test infrastructure for maintainable regression coverage where practical. Preserve stable-artifact scope, internal exclusions, baseline/report generation, and draft state. Do not alter unrelated APIs or disable enforcement to pass existing intentional 3.0 changes. Do not reply to or resolve review threads; the coordinating session handles that. Do not change the PR title or body.

@copilot Simplify this PR directly to match the core repository's existing japicmp behavior, rather than maintaining a stricter custom policy. This is a user-directed scope correction that supersedes the previous hardening assignment. The user said: "I'm not sure I want all of that complexity. I pretty much just want whatever the core repo was using."

Use https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/blob/main/buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/otel.japicmp-conventions.gradle.kts as the reference. Keep the applicable core binary/source rejection rules, cross-module classpaths and distinct archives, AutoValue handling, compatibility exclusions, and check dependency. Retain only necessary instrumentation-specific adaptations, notably stable-artifact selection, internal-package exclusions, pinned baseline/report conventions, and handling stable artifacts absent from the historical baseline. Prefer the straightforward implementation already present before commit 147f3056b6c7bd5121c6b0adc8863f305f162e50, subject to the current core reference and necessary repository-specific behavior.

Remove the custom hardening introduced in that commit: the separate 54-line SourceIncompatibleRule.kt with new-member/generic-addition analysis, the additional UNCHANGED source-rule registration, and regression fixtures that exist only to enforce behavior stricter than core. Restore core's simple source-incompatibility rule, its existing rule ordering, and its applicable exclusions. The user has deliberately chosen parity with core, including its known generic-template and inherited-abstract-method exclusions and unchanged-member limitation. Do not recreate bespoke logic to fix those known core limitations, even if review repeats them. This is not permission to disable the binary/source gate generally or remove necessary repository-specific adaptations.

Run focused validation of the simplified port, including an ordinary incompatible stable API change such as default-to-abstract or method removal being rejected and a compatible/default-method change being allowed. Restore any temporary probe edits before committing. Do not introduce new test frameworks, elaborate fixtures, or unrelated changes. Preserve the PR's draft state, base, and existing branch. Do not modify PR #20881, create another PR, or edit this PR's title/description. Do not reply to or resolve review threads; the coordinator handles review assessment and metadata.
